testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, what minimum pressure should be built up in both braking systems?
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary brake systems.

questions.question: Where should the ABS malfunction lamp be located on a dolly?
questions.explanation: A dolly with ABS must have a yellow malfunction lamp on its left side.

questions.question: When should the low air pressure warning signal turn on?

options.text: When tank pressure falls below 120 psi
When tank pressure falls below 60 psi
When tank pressure falls below 10 psi
When tank pressure falls below 5 psi

questions.correctAnswerText: When tank pressure falls below 60 psi
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning signal must turn on when air pressure in the tanks drops below 60 psi. The warning can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times
Push in the brake control knob

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, use a diamond-shaped yellow knob to control the parking brakes. Pull it out to apply the parking brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: What must you do before inspecting slack adjusters on S-cam brakes?

options.text: Park on a hill and test the brakes
Put on gloves and push in the slack adjusters
Remove the drum and look inside
Chock the wheels and disengage the parking brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Chock the wheels and disengage the parking brake
questions.explanation: Park on level ground, place wheel chocks, and disengage the parking brake before checking slack adjusters. Pull each slack adjuster to make sure it does not move more than about one inch. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the brakes
Look under the hood for an ABS sticker
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the brakes
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer has ABS, look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires connected to the brakes.

questions.question: What does the application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes
The temperature of air in the braking system
The pressure of air coming from the compressor
How many times the brakes have been used

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. Not all vehicles with air brakes have this gauge.

questions.question: How do you use the stab braking method in an emergency?

options.text: Apply full brakes until the wheels lock, release until they roll, then repeat
Apply brakes halfway while keeping the wheels rolling
Fully apply the brakes, lock the wheels, and hold until the vehicle stops

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply full brakes until the wheels lock, release until they roll, then repeat
questions.explanation: The stab braking method involves fully applying the brakes until the wheels lock. Then release the brakes until the wheels roll again. Repeat this process until the vehicle stops.

questions.question: What minimum air pressure must build up in both systems before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes?
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: What is the maximum leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: For a triple combination vehicle, the maximum safe air leakage rate during an applied leakage test is 6 psi in one minute.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?

options.text: The brakes will be very sensitive.

questions.explanation: If air pressure in an air brake system gets too low, the brakes will stop working. Pressing the brake pedal too many times can release air faster than the compressor can replace it.

questions.question: When you push the brake pedal, air brakes work:

options.text: Only if it is warm outside.

questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through the air lines to the brakes. There is usually a delay of at least one-half second between when you press the brake pedal and when the brakes start to work.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: All truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Other vehicles with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1998 must also have ABS.

questions.question: What color is the low air pressure warning light?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning light. This light is usually red and may have a buzzer to alert the driver.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, both systems share:
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system use one air compressor. If the compressor breaks, both systems will stop working.

questions.question: Why must you drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that must be drained from the tanks
To allow for a change in air pressure
To remove bad air from the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that must be drained from the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air usually contains water and compressor oil. If these build up in the system, they can damage the brakes. You must drain the tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What do anti-lock brakes do?

options.text: Help a driver avoid wheel lockup
Prevent a vehicle from accelerating while traveling uphill
Prevent a vehicle from accelerating while traveling downhill

questions.correctAnswerText: Help a driver avoid wheel lockup
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) prevent the wheels from locking up when the brakes are applied hard.

questions.question: On trucks and buses, where is the ABS malfunction lamp?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle by the passenger's door

questions.explanation: Trucks and buses with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow malfunction lamps on the instrument panel. Trailers have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the left side, at either the front or rear corner.

questions.question: What color are ABS malfunction lamps?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow malfunction lamps.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual brake system, a driver should:

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up before driving to ensure that fuel reaches the engine.
Wait until the air compressor builds up a minimum of 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
Begin driving just after the vehicle starts.
Pump the pedal about 20 times to build pressure, then begin driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the air compressor builds up a minimum of 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, wait for the air compressor to build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: What is a dual air brake system?

options.text: One air brake system with two sets of controls.
One air brake system for each side of the truck.
Two separate air brake systems with one set of controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two separate air brake systems with one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls. One system controls the rear axle brakes. The other system controls the front axle brakes.

questions.question: What must all air tanks have?
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must have drain valves. These valves remove oil and water that build up in the tanks. They can be operated by hand or automatically.

questions.question: When does brake fading happen?

options.text: When brakes are not used often enough.

questions.explanation: Using the brakes too much causes them to overheat and work less effectively. This loss of braking power is called fading.

questions.question: Which braking system uses the brake pedal?
questions.explanation: The service brake system is controlled by the brake pedal. The driver presses it to slow down or stop during normal driving.

questions.question: What happens when the S-cam turns after the brake pedal is pressed?

options.text: The brake shoes press against the inside of the brake drum.
The brake drum tightens onto the axle.
The brake lining presses against the wheel.
Air is released from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake shoes press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When the S-cam turns, it pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.
